summary:
Apollonova is a free website that turns 25 years of NASA fire satellite data into one consistent fire calendar for all 81 provinces of Turkey. MODIS (1 km pixels, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m pixels, since 2012) see the same fire differently, and raw VIIRS counts jump each time a new satellite joins, so the two records cannot be compared directly. As MODIS nears the end of its mission, its long history has to carry over to VIIRS.

We cleaned 1.39 million NASA FIRMS detections, removed industrial heat sources, filled Suomi NPP data gaps and trained a machine learning model, Anka-H, that places MODIS on the VIIRS scale. Tested on 2012–2013, years it never saw, it reaches R² 0.93 with 15% lower error than a simple sensor ratio. A second model, Anka-R, gives a fire-likelihood outlook for November and December 2026 for every ~10 km cell (ROC-AUC 0.89 for November).

Emergency teams, scientists, land managers and firefighters can explore any province, read daily and monthly fire calendars, compare years and download the data.
details:
Apollonova is a bilingual (English and Turkish) website that shows fire activity in Turkey from November 2000 to 2026 on a single, comparable scale. Users can:

- pick a province on the map, search it by name or enter coordinates;

- switch between MODIS, VIIRS and our harmonized "Combined" series;

- read a daily fire calendar for any year and a monthly calendar across all years;

- see which months were above or below the long-term median, and compare years;

- see which satellite detected what, and download every hotspot as CSV;

- explore a November–December 2026 fire-likelihood outlook by province and ~10 km cell;

- learn the basics in the Guide (a 2-minute narrated explainer video and flashcards) and check every model score on the Reports page.

1. Data: NASA FIRMS active fire products, MODIS Collection 6.1 (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS Collection 2 (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21), 1.39 million detections over Turkey.

2. Cleaning: FIRMS static-source flags remove factories and gas flares, so only vegetation fires remain. The 56 days when Suomi NPP sent no data are filled from NOAA-20, scaled to match.

3. Harmonization (Anka-H): a ratio baseline plus a HistGradientBoosting model tuned with Optuna maps MODIS counts per province and month onto the VIIRS Suomi NPP scale. Because the model is used to reconstruct the past, we test it backwards in time: trained on 2014–2026 and tested on 2012–2013. Result: R² 0.93 and 15% lower error than a simple ratio between the sensors.

4. Outlook (Anka-R): a LightGBM model tuned with Optuna estimates the chance of at least one fire hotspot in every ~10 km cell for November and December. It is tested the way it is used: for each year it is trained only on data up to October and asked to predict the next two months. On 2023–2025 it reaches ROC-AUC 0.89 for November and 0.92 for December, against 0.84 for a "same as past years" rule.

5. We compared logistic regression, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, LightGBM and XGBoost, explained the chosen models with SHAP, and dropped every idea that did not help on the validation years (extra features, a model average, probability calibration, a Poisson loss). All of this is listed openly on the Reports page.

A consistent 25-year record lets people compare today's fires with the past without false jumps caused by new satellites. Early warning and emergency teams can prepare before the riskiest weeks, land managers can plan burns and patrols with historical data, firefighters can see where and when fires cluster, and scientists get a clean, downloadable series. The project supports UN Sustainable Development Goals 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), 13 (Climate Action) and 15 (Life on Land).

- Data and machine learning: Python 3, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, Optuna, SHAP, joblib, pyarrow, matplotlib

- Data cleaning: Node.js

- Website: HTML5, CSS3 and vanilla JavaScript (ES modules) with hand-built SVG maps and charts, no framework and no build step

- Explainer video: SVG animations in the browser, Web Audio music, narration by Microsoft Edge text-to-speech voices

- Testing: pytest and Node's built-in test runner

- Hosting: Netlify

- Hardware: none beyond our own laptops

Instead of only plotting raw detections, we rebuild one continuous fire record and test it in the same direction it is used, backwards in time. The daily calendar shows a whole fire season at a glance, and the explainer video runs live in the browser in both languages instead of being a recorded file.

- Honest evaluation: every score is measured on years the model never saw and compared with a simple rule.

- Clear limits: a hotspot is a heat signal, not a confirmed fire; 2000–2011 Combined values are model estimates; the models use fire history only, without weather or vegetation data; the 2026 outlook is a likelihood, not a certainty.

- Accessibility: English and Turkish, light and dark themes, works on phones, and readable color scales.

- Openness: built only on free NASA data, with all data downloadable.
